summary.title: System Design Interview Guide for Senior Engineers
summary.one_liner: Learn how to approach a system design interview as a conversational design exercise (not a coding problem), with tips on asking clarifying questions, justifying trade-offs, and steering the interview by seniority level.
keywords: how to prepare for system design interview
how to get unstuck in interview
coding interview vs system design interview
takeaways: System design interviews are open-ended: there is no single correct answer, so justify decisions and explain how they would change under different conditions.
Ask clarifying questions about users, traffic, and limits before designing, rather than assuming the scope of a vague prompt.
Interviewers look for trade-off reasoning, a holistic view of the system and its users, and clear communication, not deep expertise in every component.
Senior candidates are expected to drive the conversation, while mid-level candidates are judged on following the interviewer's direction and avoiding talking too much.
If stuck, say so and ask for help early; admit knowledge gaps and reason from first principles.
summary.summary: This is the first part of a multi-part guide from interviewing.io on system design interviews, aimed at senior engineers. It uses essays, quotes from a former Facebook engineer and from the book Designing Your Life, and a worked example of a photo-sharing service prompt to frame system design as creative design rather than engineering optimization. It explains what interviewers evaluate (fundamentals, trade-offs, user focus) versus what does not matter (certainty, a predefined path), and gives advice on communication, handling red and green flags, and adjusting to seniority level. The page says later parts cover worked designs and how to get unstuck, but this excerpt contains no technical design content itself.
